events.text: Construction of the Mannheim Observatory began.
Construction of the Mannheim Observatory was completed.
The Mannheim Observatory ceased operation.
The observatory was established on the Königstuhl near Heidelberg.
The observatory tower was restored.
The observatory tower restoration was completed.
The tower began housing studio flats.
The Physics Institute was established in Heidelberg.
Mayer was sent to Paris to study the local water supply and astronomy.
Mayer observed the return of the comet predicted by Edmond Halley.
Mayer observed the Transit of Venus from a temporary observatory in the park of Schwetzingen Castle.
Karl Theodor decided to begin work on an observatory building on the palace roof.
The observatory building on the palace roof was inaugurated.
Mayer observed a Transit of Venus in St. Petersburg.
Mayer presented a memorandum on the construction of an observatory to the Mannheim Court.
The Elector charged the Court Chamberlain with the construction of the observatory.
The foundation stone of the tower next to Schloss Mannheim was laid.
The majority of the binary stars published in Bodes star chart were observed by Mayer.
Elector Karl Theodor left the Palatinate to govern Bavaria.
Christian Mayer died.
John Fischer resigned as Court Astronomer.
Peter Ungeschick died on the return journey from studying in Paris.
The war over the Grand Duchy of Baden's claims to areas of the Palatinate and the observatory occurred.
Roger Barry fell ill.
Roger Barry died and the observatory remained unused.
The Baden Revolution occurred.
Heinrich Christian Schumacher became Director.
Heinrich Christian Schumacher's term as Director ended.
Bernhard Nicolai became Court Astronomer.
Bernhard Nicolai died.
It was decided to end the Institute by appointing no new Court Astronomer.
The Heidelberg professor Nell took over the unpaid supervision of the institute.
The institute planned renewal with the purchase of a six-stage telescope.
Eduard Schönfeld was appointed Director of the Mannheim Observatory.
The Astronomische Gesellschaft was founded in Heidelberg.
Schönfeld served as a member of the Advisory Commission for the Transits of Venus.
Schönfeld left for Bonn and Karl Wilhelm Valentiner took over the Mannheim Directorship.
The Observatory was moved to a makeshift building in Karlsruhe.
The Großherzogliche Bergsternwarte at Königstuhl was ceremonially inaugurated.
Karl Wilhelm Valentiner retired.
Max Wolf was buried in the cemetery on the mountain.
The Mannheim instruments were donated to the State Museum of Technology and Industry in Mannheim.
The 1859 six-stage telescope was given to the city of Karlsruhe.
